newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mubarak's son steps out of shadows in advisory role.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak's son steps out of shadows in advisory role.

text.p: The son of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, an increasingly visible figure on the public scene, said on Saturday he wanted to make a contribution to policy-making but did not yet seek a political role.
Gamal Mubarak, a professional investment banker, has stepped out of the shadows in recent months in his capacity as a member of economic lobbying organisations.

He is on the executive committee of the U.S.-Egyptian Presidents' Council, an advisory body which reports straight to President Mubarak and U.S. Vice President Al Gore as part of the Partnership for Economic Cooperation and Development launched in 1994.
The council is an independent body of business executives who assist political leaders by identifying opportunities for the private sector and obstacles to its growth.
The World Economic Forum has named him as one of 100 "Global Leaders for Tomorrow" -- a nomination given prominent coverage in the government press in Egypt.
In an interview with Reuters in Davos, where he is attending the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum, Gamal Mubarak said his public activities were in fact nothing new.

"I'm very much an advocate of private-sector professionals playing a part in public life, especially in a country like Egypt which is going through a major transformation in its economic policy," he said.
Asked if he had any political ambitions, he said it was hard to separate economic policy from pure politics.
"When we sit down and discuss economic policies they do have some political implications so I'd be foolish to say politics is not of interest to me. Obviously it is.
"But in terms of seeking a political role, I would say no, definitely not at this stage in my career. I'm not considering something of that nature," he said.
"I've been in banking all my life. I love the banking world, I love the financial world and I'm thrilled to be living at this period in Egypt's history," he added.
Gamal Mubarak, who is in his late 30s, is executive director of MedInvest Associates, a small London-based financial advisory and investment banking firm.
He worked for 11 years for Bank of America until 1994, firstly in its Cairo office and later in its London office.
Mubarak, who is the president's second son, is a board member of Arab-African International Bank and of the Egyptian Centre for Economic Studies, an independent think tank.
